title: Optimization of five qPCR protocols toward the detection and the quantification of antimicrobial resistance genes in environmental samples
author: Tolosi, Carraro, et al.
materials: Sterile 1.5 ml Eppendorf style microcentrifuge tubes (Sarstedt, Germany)

Genomic DNA was extracted from the reference strains (Table 1), kindly provided by the EU Reference Laboratory for Antimicrobial Resistance (DTU, Denmark), using the Invisorb Spin Tissue Mini Kit (Invitek Molecular, Germany) according to the manufacturer's instruction. DNeasy PowerSoil kit (Qiagen, Germany) was used to extract DNA from 93 environmental samples (i.e. soil and manure) following manufacturer's instructions. Both reference strains and environmental samples were stored at -80°C and thawed in ice.Table 1List of primers and reference strains.Table 1Primer nameSequence (5’–3’)Annealing temperatureAmplicon size (bp)Ref.Reference strainsermB1CCGAACACTAGGGTTGCTC56°C139[4]E. faecalis JH2-2::Tn1545ermB2ATCTGGAACATCTGTGGTATGRTCTX-M-FCTATGGCACCACCAACGATA58°C103[7]E. coli O 149 77-30108-11RTCTX-M-RACGGCTTTCTGCCTTAGGTTFW3_CMY-2_LaheyAGACGTTTAACGGCGTGTTG58°C128[6]S. DNA quantity was assessed by using the NanoDrop spectrophotometer (ThermoScientific, USA) and Qubit 2.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA), following the manufacturer's recommendations. A260/280 values equal or higher than 1.6 were considered acceptable. The extracted DNA was stored at -20°C until qPCR analysis.

steps.title: Gather equipment and supplies
steps.instruction:
Collect the following items:
- Sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf‑style microcentrifuge tubes (Sarstedt, Germany)
- Sterile 0.5–1.5–2.0 mL Eppendorf‑style microcentrifuge tubes (Sarstedt, Germany)
- Adjustable micropipettes (0.5–1000 µL) (Gilson, USA) and (0.1–1000 µL) (Gilson, USA)
- Aerosol‑resistant micropipette tips (0.5–1000 µL) (Sarstedt, Germany) and (0.1–1000 µL) (Sarstedt, Germany)
- Vortex mixer (Velp, Italy)
- Benchtop microcentrifuge (Eppendorf, Germany) and Benchtop microcentrifuge 5424 (Eppendorf, Germany)
- Plate centrifuge 5810R (Eppendorf, Germany)
- UV‑Vis spectrophotometer NanoDrop ND‑1000 (Nanodrop Technologies, USA)
- Qubit 2.0 Fluorometer™ (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA)
- Invisorb Spin Tissue Mini Kit (Invitek Molecular, Germany)
- DNeasy PowerSoil kit (Qiagen, Germany)
- Qubit™ dsDNA HS Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA)
- LightCycler®480 (Roche, Switzerland) and LightCycler®480 software version 1.5 (Roche, Switzerland)
- Optically clear plates and foils for qPCR (Euroclone, Italy).

steps.title: Set up sterile extraction area
steps.instruction: Perform all DNA‑extraction work inside a sterile microbiological laminar‑flow cabinet to avoid contamination. Use aerosol‑resistant filter tips with all micropipettes.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the reference strains (Table 1) using the Invisorb Spin Tissue Mini Kit (Invitek Molecular, Germany) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Extract DNA from the 93 environmental samples (soil and manure) using the DNeasy PowerSoil kit (Qiagen, Germany) following the manufacturer’s protocol. After extraction, store all DNA extracts at –80 °C and thaw them on ice before downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Extract reference‑strain DNA with Invisorb Spin Tissue Mini Kit.
Extract environmental‑sample DNA with DNeasy PowerSoil kit.
Store extracts at –80 °C; thaw on ice prior to use.

steps.title: Quantify and store DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration and purity with a NanoDrop ND‑1000 spectrophotometer and a Qubit 2.0 fluorometer using the Qubit™ dsDNA HS Assay Kit, following each manufacturer’s recommendations. Accept samples with an A260/280 ratio ≥ 1.6. Store the quantified DNA at –20 °C until qPCR analysis.
